0.why: src/deinde.cpp:39, getVoltage() * the attenuator added to the 0..10 knob

comment: The whole module is four clamped straight lines off one control: out1 is four times the sweep clamped to ten, out2 the same less ten, out3 less twenty and out4 less thirty (src/deinde.cpp:39-43). The attack is linear because the sweep is linear, and the hold is the clamp. The sweep is the knob plus the jack through its attenuator, with no clamp of its own, so a large voltage can carry all four outputs to their tops at once. The maker names the Doepfer A-144 as the model, with attack-hold in place of its attack-decay. The panel prints deinde, CV in, CV, cascade, and out1 to out4, with a small diagram of the four ramps.
